messages:
alex: quick idea — I want to propose a small, explicit "loader contract" between control-plane / planner and the runtime loader. goal: decouple format negotiation (safetensors vs. legacy pt) from warmup strategy so we can stage rollouts without big if/else in runtime.

maria: high level — sounds good. can you sketch the fields? what does the handshake look like?

alex: sketch below. it's lightweight: planner calls loader.describe(model_ref) -> LoaderDescriptor. descriptor includes: format, shard_layout, recommended_warmup (none/eager/hotstart), checksum, compatibility_flags. if loader can't serve format it returns a list of compatible transforms (e.g., "convert-to-safetensors-on-the-fly").

jin: curious about on-the-fly convert. that's heavy at cold-start. we'd need async job queuing + progress reporting. we already have infra for background conversions?

sam: we do some conversions in infra but not at runtime. If loader advertises "accepts: safetensors" only, planner can route models to nodes with safetensors-enabled loaders. For fallback, planner can mark "requires_conversion": true and create a convert job before placement.

lina: can we avoid a big manifest for every model? I'd prefer a tiny descriptor that fits into placement decisions. maybe the manifest lives in object storage and descriptor has URI + small metadata.

alex: agree. descriptor example (informal):
```
{
  "format": "safetensors",
  "version": "1",
  "shard_layout": "4x-gpu-zip",
  "checksum": "sha256:abcd...",
  "warmup_hint": "hotstart",
  "compat": ["mmap-index-v2"],
  "transforms": ["quantize-int8","convert-safetensors-v1-to-v2"],
  "manifest_uri": "s3://models/foo/manifest.json"
}
```

maria: that helps. two tradeoffs I see: 1) how much intelligence on planner vs loader? planner could pick warmup policy based on warmup_hint, but runtime may override if it detects low memory. 2) compatibility_flag explosion — keep it minimal.

jin: also need to version the contract. loader/descriptor schema v1, v2, etc. otherwise rolling new loaders will break. add a top-level "contract_version" and fail-safe backcompat.

sam: what's the fallback semantics when loader says "transforms: [convert-safetensors]" but conversion fails? planner should be able to choose alternate node or return 503 with a clear error code. important for Dedicated mode.

lina: +1. define error codes: UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT, TRANSFORM_FAILED, CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES. planner can map to can_retry/can-fallback.

alex: proposed next steps: 1) short RFC doc with descriptor schema + error codes, 2) implement a thin describe() RPC on loader (handshake only, synchronous), 3) expose manifest URI and let planner schedule conversion job if needed. 4) add telemetry: format_accepted, transform_attempted, warmup_path_chosen.

maria: also add a runtime flag to opt-in to on-the-fly transforms. we shouldn't accidentally enable heavy conversions in hosted default.

jin: implementation note — keep describe() cheap: no downloads, just metadata reading and a tiny manifest parse. no heavy io.

sam: can we reuse existing shard metadata index? don't reinvent. follow same fields where applicable.

alex: yes. I'll draft RFC and reference existing index format. tagging for follow-up: @maria @jin @sam please review the schema when I post the RFC.

ci-bot: Deploy check: remember to add unit tests for describe() RPC and 3 integration tests: mismatch checksum, unsupported format fallback, and transform success path.

lina: thanks. small ask — include an example of planner pseudocode showing decision flow (format match -> warmup_hint -> schedule warmup; else if transform -> schedule convert -> then warmup). helps PMs and infra.

alex: will do. planning to open RFC tomorrow and link PRs. if no objections here, we'll treat this as the canonical follow-up to the safetensors/shard warmup threads.

maria: no objections. love the explicit contract approach. :+1:

jin: fine with that. one more: add a TTL for descriptors so we don't rely on stale metadata.

alex: good call — will add ttl_seconds and a signer field for integrity.

sam: awesome. i'll prep infra checklist for conversion jobs and monitoring.

alex: cool — thanks all. I'll post the RFC link shortly.
